subject: Multicellular organisms
justification: Multicellular organisms have multiple types of cells.

subject: Cells
justification: Cells also have specialized parts that help them do specific jobs.

subject: Leaf Cell
justification: Leaf Cell: These plant cells take in carbon dioxide from the air; using energy from the sun, they make it into sugar.

subject: Intestine Cell
justification: Intestine Cell: These cells take up nutrients from food.

subject: Neuron
justification: Neuron: These cells are part of communication pathways that go from your brain to muscles all over your body. They carry electrical signals, telling muscles when to move.

subject: Airway Cell
justification: Airway Cell: These cells are the first line of defense against anything harmful you breathe in. They fit tightly to-gether, making a barrier that keeps pathogens like viruses and bacteria out.

subject: Root Cell
object: water and minerals from the soil
justification: Root Cell: These cells are part of the outer skin of plant roots. They have a large surface area, which they use to take in water and minerals from the soil.

subject: Mitochondria
object: molecules to get energy for the cell
justification: Mitochondria: Break down molecules to get energy for the cell

subject: Nucleus
object: genetic information in the form of long, stringy DNA molecules
justification: Nucleus: Stores genetic information in the form of long, stringy DNA molecules

subject: Cilia
justification: Cilia: Move in a wave like motions. Push away mucus and trapped debris
